description: READ BACK A LINE OF REASONING, read-only: an argument for and against, an experiment's case, a paper's chain of claims, a legal case. Each claim comes with its COMPUTED truth (holds, fails or unknown), the steps that support it (rule, warrant, who confirmed them), the objections against it and how each stands (`refutes`, `stands`, `answered`), and its cited sources. Then: what the reasoning rests on and which premises cite no source, the points still contested, the disputes a Decision set to `contested` keeps open on purpose, and every claim with no support. `claim` reads under one claim; omitted, every top conclusion and contested decision. `what_this_means`: structure is not truth. Shown here, never raised as a gap. Bounded by `budget_chars`: every claim comes back whole, and a long proof pages with `next_offset`. Writes nothing. Ask for this to check an argument point by point: what backs each claim, what is disputed, and what has no evidence behind it.

budget_chars.description:
Characters the reply may spend (default 30,000). Over it, the page
returns FEWER claims, each WHOLE, never every claim with its words cut:
`next_offset` reads on, and `page` names the budget it was held to.

claim.description:
The claim to read the reasoning under: its support, what it rests on
and what stands against it, all the way down. Omitted: every top
conclusion (a node a step concludes that supports nothing further) and
every Decision set to `contested`.

limit.description:
How many claims one page returns at most (default 60, at most 500).
The walk itself always reads the whole reasoning, up to 500 records,
so the summary lists are never one page's; `capped: true` means the
WALK stopped there, and `not_walked` names what it did not read.

offset.description:
Where in the walk the page starts (default 0, the roots): pass the
reply's `next_offset` to read on. The walk's order is proof order,
breadth first from the claim asked about.
